summary: The note is a guide to a new regulatory framework for public works unveiled by the city council under Mayor Elizabeth Thompson on October 15, 2023. It walks through each project stage: planning and approvals, funding, procurement, construction oversight, legal and safety compliance, monitoring and reporting, and public involvement. Local projects such as the Hazelwood intersection, Riverside Park and Broadway Bridge illustrate the rules in practice.
one_line: Guide to the city's new public works regulatory framework, covering planning, funding, procurement, oversight, compliance, reporting and public participation.
key_facts: The city council, led by Mayor Elizabeth Thompson, unveiled the new public works regulatory framework on October 15, 2023, to improve efficiency, transparency and effectiveness.
As of September 1, 2023, all public works projects must undergo a Public Needs & Impact Assessment (PNIA).

Planners must follow zoning laws, building codes and the recently established Environmental Compliance Checklist (ECC); the Hazelwood Traffic Intersection Expansion had to reevaluate designs to meet updated environmental standards.
City Treasurer Michelle Rodriguez introduced the Financial Accountability & Transparency (FAT) protocol on November 3, 2023, covering funding via federal grants, local taxes, bonds, or a combination.

Project budgets need approval from both the Local Financial Oversight Committee (LFOC) and the Public Works Regulatory Board (PWRB); the Riverside Park Renovation Project, about $6 million, was vetted by both.
The Local Government Procurement Guidelines (LGPG), updated December 12, 2023, mandate competitive bidding for all public works projects and include provisions favoring local businesses.
The Northwest Water Treatment Plant upgrade features local raw materials and labor in line with LGPG policies.
The Department of Public Works Oversight (DPWO) has had a new mandate since March 5, 2024, to ensure contractors meet specifications, with regular inspections and audits.
Susan Clark oversees the East Side Road Expansion and reports to the DPWO, the Local Government Body (LGB) and community stakeholders.
Non-compliant projects face corrective actions, fines or construction halts; the April 2024 Broadway Bridge safety violations led to stringent reevaluation before work resumed.
The Access to Public Works Information Act (APWIA), championed by Councilwoman Sarah Jennings and ratified September 29, 2023, requires publishing meeting minutes, expense reports and status updates.
Citizen advisory groups and independent auditors take part in monitoring; the Grand Stadium Expansion has stayed on schedule and budget.
Public input led to the redesign of the Lincoln District Community Center to accommodate more youth services.
